limitations: No tests/builds were executed in this review.
The generic module_io rank routines are selected verbatim and run, but the full module_io module is not built or linked.
MPI behavior is a fixture broadcast, not actual WRF I/O decomposition.
The workflow directly invokes the Python fixture in standalone-columns; the NetCDF ZZ fixture itself is not registered as a CTest in the shown CMake changes.

reviewed_changes.finding: The fixture writes two different sentinel records at 00:00 and 01:00, confirms the low-level Time dimension ID is the unlimited dimension, checks its length is 2, then reads and validates the corresponding data at both dates.
reviewed_changes.item: Unlimited time dimension and multi-record readback

reviewed_changes.finding: For both REAL4-on-output variables, the fixture reads as WRF_REAL and WRF_DOUBLE. It compares the double read with exact promotion of the read REAL4 values; the DOUBLE write uses representable half increments and checks the REAL4 result against conversion.
A read using QQ must return WRF_WARN_BAD_MEMORYORDER; a subsequent valid lowercase zz read of the second record is checked exactly.

The Python harness extracts the actual dim_from_memorder and lower_case subroutines from the pinned module_io.F source, compiles them with the fixture, and checks uppercase/lowercase ZZ rank 2 plus XY, XYZ, and rejected QQ behavior. The receipt labels this as selected helper execution, not full module_io runtime.

Integer, REAL, and DOUBLE-to-REAL4 writes; uppercase/lowercase ZZ; a 3x5 nonsquare ordered sentinel; names/extents/rank metadata; absence of unsupported variable; and nonspatial helper behavior remain asserted.

The runner pins module_io.F and test/backend sources before use, runs O0 and O2, journals child return codes, and checks test success markers; optional MPI mode exercises monitor/backend/broadcast fixture behavior rather than full WRF module_io.
